title: The School
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Use the school's own motto, values and stories. The teacher supplies the school's values; questions use common ones.

skills.key_step: The child names the value a school situation shows (respect, honesty, responsibility, hard work, unity, cleanliness) and says why it matters.

floor.prerequisite: Names a responsibility of a learner at school.
floor.question: Give one responsibility you have at school.
floor.answer: any of: keep the class clean, do homework, respect others

representations: short story cards of school situations
the school notice board with values and motto
a value badge for the week
steps: Say how the school is better for it.
contexts: helping a new learner find the classroom
sweeping the class on duty day

board.do: Write: "Wanjiru found 50 shillings and gave it to the teacher."
Point at "gave it to the teacher".
Write honesty and one reason it matters.

misconceptions.ask: Wekesa finds a lost shilling coin and hands it to the teacher. Which value does he show?
misconceptions.repair: Make cards of the value words and match them to six short scenes.

misconceptions.ask: Which is a value of a school?
misconceptions.repair: Ask the child what a value is: a good idea that guides us, even without a teacher watching.

misconceptions.ask: Juma picks up litter when no teacher is near. Is he showing a value?
misconceptions.repair: Ask whether the compound is cleaner whether or not a teacher saw it.

listen_for: Yes, it is a rule we are punished for breaking
misconceptions.ask: Our motto is "Strive to excel". Is the motto a school rule?
misconceptions.repair: Read the notice board together and sort: motto, values, rules.

checks.question: A learner owns up to breaking a window. Which value does this show?
Is a value the same as a punishment?
checks.answer: No: a value is a quality we show; a punishment follows breaking a rule
